## Where the lab will live

The Crossplane lab will be authored as a **reusable, cross-course
lab** — the same pattern the Pico course uses for its shared Hello
Pico lab — so that other courses can point at it too. When it lands,
you will complete it by opening the shared lab page and following the
walkthrough, exactly like the
[Hello Pico lab](../../../../labs/hello-pico/index.html) works today.

## Target environment

The lab will target **local minikube** as its reference Kubernetes
environment:

- Small enough to run on a laptop — matches the academy's expectation
  of a local runnable environment.
- Provides the full Kubernetes control plane, which is what Crossplane
  extends. A container-only runtime is not enough — Crossplane needs a
  real control plane to install the Provider and reconcile Managed
  Resources against.
- Version pins for `minikube`, the Kubernetes control plane, and the
  Crossplane Provider will be declared on the lab's Prerequisites page,
  per the Runnable Academy Contract §2.

## What you will produce (once the lab is published)

- A running local **minikube** cluster with **Crossplane** installed.
- The **Kubernetes Provider** installed via a Crossplane `Provider`
  resource.
- An **XRD** for `HelloWorldPico` and a **Composition** that turns any
  `HelloWorldPico` XR into concrete Kubernetes resources.
- A **Composite Resource** carrying the same greeting value you used in
  the Pico lab, reconciled into Kubernetes resources that together
  print `Hello, Pico!` from inside the cluster.
- The course-scoped artifact
  `hello-world-pico-on-kubernetes` (matching the `produces:` entry in
  [`courses/crossplane/metadata.yaml`](../../metadata.yaml)).

## What to do while the lab is not yet published

- Complete the reusable
  [Hello Pico lab](../../../../labs/hello-pico/index.html) to produce
  the `hello-world-pico` artifact this lab will consume as its
  greeting input.
- Work through the [Exercise](exercise.qmd) on this lesson to lock in
  the mapping from the Pico pipeline onto Crossplane primitives.
- Install local minikube ahead of time if you want to be ready — the
  upstream install guide is at
  <https://minikube.sigs.k8s.io/docs/start/>. Version pins will be
  published on the lab's Prerequisites page when it lands.
